timings.caption: I'm Maya. As my life changes, I keep building on one health history.
2022: I'm tired after work. I start with my period history and the records I already have.
I bring in the original result. Its date and findings are there to check, not silently accept.
I confirm the date and choose shared notebooks. One source can belong in more than one part of my care.
My period dates and iron plan become things I can follow through on. I review an entry before confirming it.
A saved, scripted visit and my own notes sit beside the record. I can replay it and keep what matters to me.
2024–25: fertility investigations lead to IVF, pregnancy and becoming a parent. I don't start my history over.
I add Fertility and IVF to the same library. The original treatment records stay available.
The dose, schedule and dates come from the treatment record. I can distinguish the plan from what I actually log.
When several medicines are due together, I review the selection and date, then confirm the entries together.
A check-in can wait until tomorrow. A confirmed appointment stays different from a plan.
For one question, I inspect a saved explanation and the original source. Retrieved, mature, fertilized and frozen are different stages.
Pregnancy and postpartum care join the same history. The estimated due date stays separate from the confirmed birth.
2026: my periods have returned. I can look back across five years while finding a routine that fits life now.
The latest review is still linked to its dated original. Earlier notebooks and notes have not disappeared.
A course has a calculated supply and a planned end date. My own activity goal is a separate choice.
I review Maya's documented measurements directly: chart, source dates and table. Nothing is invented to fill an empty category.
Now try a fresh reading of your own. Your camera test stays separate from my sample history.
Pause here to try the prototype. Rest, face the light, and choose Start when you're ready. Video stays on your device.
This recording environment has no physical camera. The real recovery state stays visible; sample values are not passed off as live inference.
Close stops capture. A supported estimate can be reviewed and kept in its own test session, then cleared.
From a first concern to changing treatment and a new routine, I have grown my history—not replaced it.
